t: Peter the Great founded the city on 27 May 1703 on land taken from Sweden, using conscripted serfs, and moved the capital there in 1712.
It was the seat of the Russian court and government for most of the time until 1918, and the revolutions of 1905 and 1917 began there before the Bolsheviks moved the government to Moscow in 1918.
It was renamed Petrograd in 1914 and Leningrad in 1924, survived a siege of 872 days from 1941 to 1944, and took back the name Saint Petersburg in 1991.
dyk: In 1914 Tsar Nicholas II renamed the city Petrograd to remove the German words Sankt and Burg from its name. It became Leningrad in 1924, and a referendum in 1991 restored the name Saint Petersburg.
ev: Peter the Great captures Nyenskans and lays down the Peter and Paul Fortress
Peter moves the capital from Moscow to Saint Petersburg
The Decembrist revolt takes place on Senate Square
The emancipation of the serfs brings a large influx of former peasants into the capital
The Bolsheviks storm the Winter Palace in the October Revolution
Lenin moves the Soviet government to Moscow
German forces begin the siege of Leningrad, which lasts until 1944
A referendum restores the name Saint Petersburg

f.founded: On 27 May 1703 (16 May in the Julian calendar) by Tsar Peter the Great, who laid down the Peter and Paul Fortress on Zayachy (Hare) Island after capturing the Swedish fortress of Nyenskans.
f.where: On the Neva River at the head of the Gulf of Finland on the Baltic Sea, on the islands of the river's delta and the lowlands along Neva Bay, in north-western Russia.
f.known: Peter the Great's founding on a captured Swedish site; capital of the Russian Empire; the Winter Palace and the Hermitage; the Decembrist revolt of 1825; the revolutions of 1905 and 1917; the siege of Leningrad of 1941 to 1944; its canals and bridges
f.today: Saint Petersburg is the second-largest city in Russia, after Moscow, and is governed as a federal city.
